summary: Round 11 is done. I built R35b, built all five R38 items with tests, and ran the one arm of the final tree (R37b + R35b + R38, src hash 4c9d17a9) against round-10/arm-final on all 15 sweep-9 hand-overs. Compared with that base: workers at winter rose from 222 to 243 (7 colonies better, 8 worse), viable colonies from 10 to 13, and the kitchen door went from 1 to 3 of 3 viable. Median protein intake over need rose from 0.298 to 0.329, still well under the 0.7 bar. Larvae starved fell from 16 to 10, and predation deaths fell from 22 to 0, so R37's bar is met. Brood hygiene deaths rose from 31 to 60; I measured that loss but did not fix it. R35b on its own four-colony arm changed no protein: two of its runs are identical to the base, because in these colonies the protein share sP is already at or above the protein need. Each fix has a unit test that fails on the old rule. Typecheck is clean, and the red tests left are all known or also red on HEAD. Progress and results are in docs/design/tasks/colony-life-ledger.md under '## Round 11' and '### Round 11 results'.
causesRanked: 1. Protein not found: an entered prey patch was never learnt (kd #1: 14 worker-seconds inside in 4 game days, no prey spawned, nothing noticed). A 4 P carcass 60 BU from kd #2's door had foragers and tenders inside its odour for 142 s and stayed unknown, because only a scout or a forager collecting could make a source known. Scouts had fallen to 0.02-0.1 by day 5. Fixed by R38 items 1, 2, 3 and 5: we #1 protein 0.064 -> 0.506, kd #2 0.037 -> 0.318; kd #1, kd #2, we #1, cpv #3 and sg #3 became viable.

2. Carry form of carrion: on kd #1 the ants took 24 loads at 0.24 P each (5.8 P) from a 120 P carcass before it rotted, and trips did continue until it was a husk. Fixed by R38 item 4: large-carcass protein brought home 3.2 -> 15.0.
3. Predation: 22 deaths in the base arm, 0 now. This is R37b's measurement (built in round 10, measured here).

4. Brood hygiene, the largest new loss (31 -> 60): the first cohort pupates all at once and leaves 6-9 meconium items in one chamber against a tolerance of 3, and each dead brood adds a corpse. The one hauler on cpv #2 stood outside, stopped by the rule that keeps ants out of a wet nest, in 58 of the 74 dirty hours. Measured only.
5. Protein fell where colonies now forage more sugar: cpv #1 0.41 -> 0.25, cpv #3 0.52 -> 0.31, sg #3 0.62 -> 0.47, with carbohydrate up in each. Not fixed.

notesForIntegrator: R38 is built and measured. Bars against arm-final: kitchen door viable >= 2 of 3 is met (3 of 3). Median protein >= 0.7 is not met (0.329). 'No archetype worse' fails on playground-park, 3 -> 2: pp #3 has 20 workers but carbohydrate in store is 0.92 of R27's winter need. R37's predation bar is met (0 deaths).
R35b moved no protein: in these colonies sP is already at or above needP (kd #1 probe: sP 0.75-0.88 against needP 0.75-0.84), so the change rarely binds. I kept it as ruled; it does no harm.

Decisions you may want to rule on: (1) the missing-nutrient scouts are served after the hygiene haul when brood lies among waste, i.e. after all brood care rather than strictly 'directly after nurse and queen-care'. (2) The small-colony rule still asks 2 scouts at 6 workers, so the '6 workers -> 1' test checks the floor on its own. (3) A herd found by its sign, a patch noticed, or smelled food reported changes only colony knowledge; spawning is unchanged. Smelled food is reported when the worker is back in the nest, through the same news path as a scout's return. (4) The smelled-food rule applies to every food kind, so colonies also learn more sugar; this is likely why protein fell in cpv #1, cpv #3 and sg #3.
